_comment.what: Merged by init into the project's .claude/settings.json. The installer strips this _comment key. Hooks are NOT here; the plugin's hooks.json supplies them.
_comment.{test_command}: The stack's test command, for example 'python3 -m pytest' or 'pnpm test'. Becomes an allow rule with a trailing wildcard.
_comment.{lint_command}: The stack's lint command, same treatment.
_comment.{typecheck_command}: The stack's type-check command, same treatment.
_comment.{format_command}: The stack's format command, same treatment.
_comment.{package_domains}: One array element. init replaces it with the stack's registry hosts: python pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org; node registry.npmjs.org; go proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org; rust crates.io, index.crates.io and static.crates.io.
_comment.{install_command}: The stack's install prefix (pip install, npm install, cargo add, go get). Becomes an ask rule.
_comment.{cleanup_days}: cleanupPeriodDays, whole number of at least 1; the team chooses. Default 30.
_comment.notes: DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL are deliberately not pinned: settings env overwrites the shell and would override a repo's own test configuration (a conftest default, for example). sandbox.filesystem.denyRead does not stop the Read tool, so the Read deny rules below repeat the credential paths. sandbox.network.allowedDomains does not limit WebFetch, which is why WebFetch is on the ask list. gh and docker compose are excluded from the sandbox because they fail under it (TLS verification on macOS, docker is incompatible); they then run with full access, and permissions.deny still blocks gh pr merge. Smoke tests against a server on the host work on macOS through allowLocalBinding; on Linux run them from a human terminal. Real env files are denied by explicit name (.env, .env.local, .env.development, .env.production, .env.staging, .env.test, .env.*.local, *.env) and never by a .env* wildcard, so .env.example, .env.sample, .env.template and .env.dist stay readable for tests and verify. Override paths for .env variants if the project uses other names. sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite holds only uv's cache (~/.cache/uv): every `uv run` (the graph plugin's `uv run --project <plugin root> sdlc-graph ...`, and `uv run pytest` in a uv project) opens its cache for writing first and exits 2 with 'Failed to initialize cache' under the sandbox without it (probed on Claude Code 2.1.316). The plugin root is deliberately not writable (it holds the hook scripts): the graph's .venv there is created by its MCP server, which starts outside the sandbox when the session opens. A team that sets UV_CACHE_DIR replaces this path with its own.
_comment.{plugin_root}: The plugin's installed directory (init's own plugin root). Fills the rules that pre-approve the plugin's scripts in the exact form the skills run them, python3 -I "<root>/scripts/<name>" and bash "<root>/scripts/<name>"; with no value the rules are dropped. The root moves when the plugin updates, so re-run init after an update. check_skill_permissions.py proves these rules cover every command a skill names.
